solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boozy yob, exceptionally large, joining group outside university

indicators.note: something done exceptionally departs from the normal way, so the letters leave their usual order
one word standing outside another wraps around it, holding it within

blocks.note: the letters of this word rearranged
a lot is a group or batch of things
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A huge drunken thug falls in with a gang that hangs about outside the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged word comes first, then the group wraps round the university letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lager lout is a British term for a young man made rowdy and aggressive by drinking beer.

clue.text: Innocent little creatures losing heart in workplaces

indicators.note: losing the heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: young sheep, proverbially innocent

explanation.surface: Gentle young animals grow dispirited inside factories or offices.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter M goes from the five-letter word for young sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Labs, short for laboratories, are rooms where scientists do their work.

clue.text: Ship that's gone out to save everyone

indicators.note: letters put out of place are no longer in their original order
to save something is to hold it safely inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: the letters of this word rearranged
all means every person

explanation.surface: A rescue vessel has set off to bring everybody to safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone out' looks like a description of the ship departing, but 'out' scrambles 'gone' and the result goes round ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large sailing ship of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Regret the way of Napoleon

blocks.note: first meaning: to feel sorry about something
second meaning: the French word for a street, as Napoleon would say

explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon stands for France, so 'the way' is a road in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The English verb means to be sorry for, and the identically spelt French noun means a street.

clue.text: Eight days of celebration in month on avenue

blocks.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
AVE is the street-sign abbreviation for avenue

explanation.surface: A week-long festival is held one month along a city avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the month sits over the avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church calendar an octave is the eight-day period of observance following a major feast.

clue.text: Elgar isn't bad — do they tinkle in his music?

definitions.text: do they tinkle in his music

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoilt and out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the composer's name and the contraction, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Defending Elgar's music while wondering whether percussion pings away in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't bad' reads as praise for the composer, but 'bad' is the anagram signal and 'isn't' supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are small metal percussion instruments that ring with a high tinkling note in an orchestra.

clue.text: Last bit of resistance of retreating enemy

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is just its final letter
retreating means going backwards, so everything before it is read in reverse

blocks.note: the final letter of this word; that it then runs on into the next word is a coincidence of the selection, not a hidden word
taken as written

explanation.surface: The final pocket of resistance from an enemy army in retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The small word 'of' is wordplay, not grammar: the last letter of resistance plus 'of' is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe is an adversary or enemy.

clue.text: Found different ballet movement

indicators.note: making the word different means putting its letters in another order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone discovered a new step in dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondu is a ballet term for a lowering of the body by bending the supporting leg.

clue.text: Serious listener has comfortable home

blocks.note: the ear is the organ that listens
a nest is a snug, cosy home

explanation.surface: A grave-minded person who pays attention lives in a cosy house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listener' is the usual crossword trick for the body part that hears.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes someone sincere and intensely serious in manner.

clue.text: Most audacious and better than the rest — mature within

indicators.note: within places one word inside the other

blocks.note: the best is superior to all others
mature can mean grown old

explanation.surface: Praise for the most daring and outstanding person, who is also grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Boldest is the superlative of bold, meaning the most daring or brazen.

clue.text: Interior of pub — about to be done over

indicators.note: something done over is turned over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
RE means about or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: The inside of a pub is about to be redecorated or wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done over' sounds like a refurbishment or a beating, but it turns the word for about backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner, as an adjective, describes what is on the inside, the interior part.

clue.text: Maybe a time before Christmas by Yorkshire river

blocks.note: per means by, as in per post
Advent is the church season leading up to Christmas
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Perhaps a pre-Christmas visit to a riverside in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in a different order: 'by' comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an archaic adverb meaning perhaps or by chance.

clue.text: Female performers, experts concealing long hair

indicators.note: concealing something means hiding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: aces are people highly skilled at something
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Skilled stage women hiding their flowing hair, perhaps under wigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Actresses are women who perform roles on stage or screen.

clue.text: Eastern money consumed for legislative body

blocks.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Far Eastern countries
past tense of eat

explanation.surface: Oriental cash being swallowed up by a parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern' looks like it gives E, but it belongs with 'money' to name an Asian coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is the upper house of a parliament or other law-making assembly.

clue.text: Old Bob ill, out on the briny?

blocks.note: a bob was an old British shilling, abbreviated s
ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: Elderly Bob is unwell and not at home, maybe away at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is pre-decimal slang for a shilling, written s; it is not a man's name here. The briny is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing means travelling across water by boat, so a sailor is literally out on the sea.

clue.text: Bishop with lamp maybe revealing plant disease

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a lamp is an example of a light

explanation.surface: A cleric holding a lantern uncovers disease among the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Blight is a fungal or bacterial disease that withers plants, as in potato blight.

clue.text: Attractiveness of heartless girl having secret affair

indicators.note: without its heart a word keeps only its outside letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
an amour is a love affair, often a clandestine one

explanation.surface: The allure of a cold-hearted woman conducting a hidden romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is the glittering allure or charm that makes someone attractive.

clue.text: Capone with bear turning up for fair game?

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters run upwards, so they are read in reverse

blocks.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
Winnie-the-Pooh, the famous bear

explanation.surface: A gangster with a bear appearing at a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Both names together are reversed in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a fairground game in which players throw rings over prizes to win them.

clue.text: Having much responsibility, like a driver with warm bottom?

definitions.text: like a driver with warm bottom

blocks.note: first meaning: idiomatically, facing pressure and having to make difficult decisions

blocks.clueFragment: like a driver with warm bottom
blocks.note: second meaning, taken literally: occupying a heated car seat

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the idiom literally; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in a position of pressure and accountability, while the literal reading suits a motorist on a heated seat.

clue.text: Thunderous god descending on knight, old character

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming down on something means sitting above it, so the first piece goes on top

blocks.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A deity of thunder swoops down upon a knight, an ancient figure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'descending on' puts the god above the knight. 'Character' means a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn is a letter of the Old English runic alphabet, written þ, representing the th sound.

clue.text: Fellows had briefly to be put right

blocks.note: fellows are men
had shortened to the contraction 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: Some chaps had to be corrected, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend is to repair, putting something back in working order.

clue.text: False gods, surprisingly solid

indicators.note: something turning out surprisingly is not as expected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Graven images of pagan deities turn out to be unexpectedly sturdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idols are images worshipped as gods, the biblical false gods.

clue.text: Accommodation given to king and one Italian boss

blocks.note: a pad is slang for a flat or place to live
R for rex, Latin for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lodgings are provided for a monarch and a Mafia chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Padrone is Italian for master or employer, used in English for an Italian proprietor or boss.

clue.text: Point made by little Dorothy

blocks.note: first meaning: a small round mark
second meaning: a pet-name shortening of Dorothy

explanation.walkthrough: 'little' here means a diminutive form of the name, not a small girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a tiny spot or full stop and a familiar short form of the name Dorothy.

clue.text: Some burning inside to get drink

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A burning sensation inside after a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin is a spirit flavoured with juniper berries.

clue.text: Very tired journalists finally meeting mad man (editor)

indicators.note: finally points to just the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the final letter of this word
the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Exhausted reporters at last interviewing a crazed newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As mad as a hatter' is the proverbial phrase behind the mad man. Shattered is British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattered is informal British for utterly exhausted, worn out completely.
